title.en: Opening a web page: with no DNS, and over one connection (R2 · 4, 5)
title.zh: 打开一个网页：没有 DNS，以及只用一条连接（复2 · 4、5）

description.en: What DNS does and what still works without it; how a page is fetched over TCP, what a persistent connection saves in round trips, and the catch of deciding when to close it.
description.zh: DNS 做什么，没了它还有什么能用；网页是怎样通过 TCP 取回来的，持久连接省下多少往返，以及什么时候关连接这个难处。

name.en: What DNS is for: translating domain names to IP addresses (name resolution)
name.zh: DNS 的作用：把域名翻译成 IP 地址 (name resolution)

name.en: The DNS name resolution process and caching
name.zh: DNS 解析过程与缓存 (DNS name resolution process and caching)

name.en: Zones and zone name servers, and why not centralise
name.zh: 区与区名字服务器，为什么不集中 (zones, zone name servers, why not centralise)
非持久 HTTP 与往返时间 (non-persistent HTTP, RTT)
持久 HTTP 与流水线 (persistent HTTP, pipelining)

description.en: Thinking the Internet itself stops working without DNS
description.zh: 以为没有 DNS，互联网本身就停了

description.en: Counting round trips without the TCP handshake
description.zh: 数往返时忘了 TCP 握手

paras.en: Consider a situation in which a cyberterrorist makes all the DNS servers in the world crash simultaneously. How does this change one's ability to use the Internet?
paras.zh: 设想一个网络恐怖分子让全世界的 DNS 服务器同时崩溃。这会怎样改变人们使用互联网的能力？

text.en: Reading it slowly
text.zh: 慢慢读一遍

items.en: **DNS** (the Domain Name System) is the service that turns names such as www.unimelb.edu.au into IP addresses. It is built below from the ground up.
items.zh: **DNS**（Domain Name System，域名系统）是把 www.unimelb.edu.au 这样的名字翻译成 IP 地址的服务。下面从头讲。

items.en: **All the DNS servers in the world, simultaneously**: every name server, from the root servers to your provider's local one, at once. No other name server is left to fall back on.
items.zh: **全世界所有的 DNS 服务器，同时**：从根服务器到你网络服务商的本地服务器，全部一起。没有任何别的域名服务器可以兜底。

items.en: **How does this change one's ability to use the Internet**: what stops working, what still works, and what that means for an ordinary user.
items.zh: **怎样改变使用互联网的能力**：什么停了，什么还能用，这对普通用户意味着什么。

text.en: The ideas: what DNS does and who uses it; how a lookup works; and which parts of the Internet never ask DNS at all.
text.zh: 需要的想法：DNS 做什么、谁在用它；一次查询是怎么完成的；以及互联网的哪些部分根本不找 DNS。

text.en: Packets are addressed by IP address, such as 121.7.106.83. People use names, such as www.google.com. DNS translates between them: **name resolution** finds the IP address for a host name. Opening www.someschool.edu/index.html, as the course's slide walks through it:
text.zh: 包是按 IP 地址寻址的，比如 121.7.106.83。人用的是名字，比如 www.google.com。DNS 负责在两者之间翻译：**域名解析**（name resolution）为一个主机名找到它的 IP 地址。打开 www.someschool.edu/index.html 时，按课件的步骤：

items.en: The browser takes the host name, www.someschool.edu, out of the URL and hands it to the DNS client on the same machine.
items.zh: 浏览器从 URL 里取出主机名 www.someschool.edu，交给本机的 DNS 客户端。

items.en: The DNS client sends a query with the name to a DNS server, and eventually receives a reply with the IP address.
items.zh: DNS 客户端把名字放进一个查询发给 DNS 服务器，最后收到带着 IP 地址的回复。

items.en: Only now can the browser open a TCP connection to port 80 at that address.
items.zh: 直到这时，浏览器才能向这个地址的 80 端口建立 TCP 连接。

text.en: Almost everything that starts from a name uses DNS: the browser for every new site, a mail server to find where to deliver mail for a domain (its mail server record), most apps for their servers.
text.zh: 几乎一切从名字出发的事都要用 DNS：浏览器每打开一个新网站，邮件服务器为某个域名找投递地址（它的邮件服务器记录），大多数应用找自己的服务器。

text.en: DNS is a distributed database arranged as a tree. **Root name servers** know the servers of the top-level domains; **top-level domain servers** (com, edu, au and so on) know the servers of the zones below them; each organisation's **authoritative name servers** know its own hosts. Your provider's **local name server** does the asking for you and **caches** each answer for a while (every record carries a time to live, TTL).
text.zh: DNS 是一个排成树形的分布式数据库。**根域名服务器**知道各顶级域的服务器；**顶级域服务器**（com、edu、au 等）知道它下面各区域的服务器；每个机构的**权威域名服务器**知道自己的主机。你的网络服务商的**本地域名服务器**替你去问，并把每个答案**缓存**一段时间（每条记录都带着生存时间 TTL）。

alt.en: Your computer asks the local name server (1). The local name server asks the root (2), edu (4), washington.edu (6) and cs.washington.edu (8); each of the first three replies with a referral (3, 5, 7), and the last with the address (9), which goes back to your computer (10).
alt.zh: 你的电脑问本地域名服务器 (1)。本地域名服务器依次问根 (2)、edu (4)、washington.edu (6)、cs.washington.edu (8)；前三个各回复一个“去问谁”的指引 (3, 5, 7)，最后一个回复地址 (9)，地址再送回你的电脑 (10)。

caption.en: Looking up robot.cs.washington.edu, as in the course's slide: the local name server walks down the tree, one referral at a time, until a server knows the address.
caption.zh: 查询 robot.cs.washington.edu，和课件里一样：本地域名服务器沿着树往下走，一次一个指引，直到某台服务器知道这个地址。

title.en: What breaks, and what does not

text.en: Go through the layers. Does anything below the application layer need DNS? Routers forward packets by IP address; TCP connects to an IP address and a port; neither ever asks DNS. So **the network itself keeps working**: packets still flow to any address.
text.zh: 一层一层地看。应用层以下有谁需要 DNS 吗？路由器按 IP 地址转发包；TCP 连接的是 IP 地址加端口；它们从不找 DNS。所以**网络本身照常工作**：包照样能送到任何地址。

text.en: What breaks is one step: **name → address**. A browser given www.unimelb.edu.au cannot find the server; an email to someone at unimelb.edu.au cannot find the mail server. You could still reach a server by typing its IP address instead of its name, but people do not know the addresses of the services they use (and the addresses change).
text.zh: 坏掉的是一步：**名字 → 地址**。浏览器拿着 www.unimelb.edu.au 找不到服务器；发给 unimelb.edu.au 某人的邮件找不到邮件服务器。你仍然可以输入 IP 地址代替名字去访问服务器，可人们并不知道自己用的那些服务的地址（而且地址还会变）。

text.en: So: possible in principle, nearly impossible in practice for most users.
text.zh: 所以：原则上还能用，实际上对大多数人几乎没法用。

prompt.en: All DNS servers have crashed. Which of these still works?
prompt.zh: 所有 DNS 服务器都崩溃了。下面哪个还能正常进行？

label.en: A video call that was already connected
label.zh: 一个早已接通的视频通话

label.en: Sending an email to a friend at another university
label.zh: 给另一所大学的朋友发邮件

feedback.en: Your mail server must look up the mail server of your friend's domain, which needs DNS.
feedback.zh: 你的邮件服务器得查朋友那个域名的邮件服务器，这需要 DNS。

label.en: Opening a news site you have never visited
label.zh: 打开一个从没去过的新闻网站

feedback.en: A new name has never been looked up, so no cache holds its address.
feedback.zh: 新名字从没查过，没有哪个缓存里有它的地址。

explain.en: The call's addresses were found before the crash, and packets between them need only IP and TCP or UDP. Anything that still has to turn a name into an address stops.
explain.zh: 通话双方的地址是在崩溃之前就查好的，它们之间的包只需要 IP 和 TCP 或 UDP。凡是还得把名字翻译成地址的事，都停了。

title.zh: 复习课 (2) 第 4 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: DNS maps human-readable domain names to IP addresses. If all DNS servers crashed, domain names could no longer be resolved, although IP routing and transport connections do not depend on DNS, so packets would still be delivered to IP addresses. Web pages could then only be reached by typing the IP address of the server instead of its domain name (and email could not be delivered, since finding a domain's mail server needs DNS). Since most users do not know the IP addresses of the servers they use, the Internet would become extremely inefficient, if not virtually impossible, to use for most people.
paras.zh: DNS 把人能读懂的域名映射成 IP 地址。如果所有 DNS 服务器都崩溃，域名将无法解析；但 IP 路由和传输层连接并不依赖 DNS，所以包照样能送到 IP 地址。这时只能输入服务器的 IP 地址而不是域名来访问网页（邮件也投递不了，因为找一个域的邮件服务器需要 DNS）。由于大多数用户不知道自己所用服务器的 IP 地址，对大多数人来说，互联网会变得极其低效，甚至几乎无法使用。

text.en: Where the marks are: what DNS does; that the network still works by address; the practical consequence for users. *The Internet stops* is wrong, and loses the mark for understanding what DNS is.
text.zh: 分在这些地方：DNS 做什么；网络按地址照常工作；对用户的实际后果。写“互联网停了”是错的，也就丢了“懂得 DNS 是什么”的那一分。

summary.en: Beyond the exam: the caches would buy some hours
summary.zh: 超出考试：缓存还能撑几个小时

text.en: Answers already cached, in your computer, your browser or your provider's local name server, keep working until their TTL runs out, which ranges from minutes to a day. So the failure would spread over hours as caches emptied. The real DNS is built against this: the 13 root server identities are each served by many machines around the world.
text.zh: 已经缓存了的答案（在你的电脑、浏览器或网络服务商的本地域名服务器里）在 TTL 用完之前照样有效，从几分钟到一天不等。所以故障会随着缓存一个个过期，在几个小时里逐渐蔓延。真实的 DNS 早就防着这一点：13 个根服务器标识，每一个背后都是分布在世界各地的许多台机器。

paras.en: What are the benefits of persistent HTTP connections, and what is the main challenge associated with them?
paras.zh: 持久 HTTP 连接有什么好处？与之相关的主要难点是什么？

text.en: Reading it slowly
text.zh: 慢慢读一遍

items.en: **HTTP**: the browser (the client) asks a web server for *objects* (the HTML file, each image, each script), one request and one response per object, carried over TCP.
items.zh: **HTTP**：浏览器（客户端）向网页服务器请求*对象*（HTML 文件、每张图片、每个脚本），每个对象一个请求、一个响应，用 TCP 运送。

items.en: **Persistent** or not: whether one TCP connection carries one object, or many.
items.zh: **持久**与否：一条 TCP 连接只运送一个对象，还是运送很多个。

items.en: The question asks for *benefits*, plural, and *the main challenge*, one.
items.zh: 题目问的是*好处*（复数），以及*主要难点*（一个）。

text.en: The ideas: how a page is fetched, what each TCP connection costs in round trips and resources, and why keeping a connection open raises the question of when to close it.
text.zh: 需要的想法：网页是怎么取回来的，每条 TCP 连接在往返和资源上要花多少，以及为什么一旦保持连接，就要面对什么时候关的问题。

title.en: One connection per object, or one for all
title.zh: 每个对象一条连接，还是全都走一条

text.en: A web page is a base HTML file plus the objects it refers to. The course's example: home.html with 10 JPEG images, 11 objects in all, all on the same server.
text.zh: 一个网页是一个基础 HTML 文件，加上它引用的各个对象。课上的例子：home.html 带 10 张 JPEG 图片，一共 11 个对象，都在同一台服务器上。

text.en: **Non-persistent HTTP**: each object gets a TCP connection of its own. Open it (one round trip for the handshake), send the request and get the first bytes back (a second round trip, plus the time to transmit the file), close it. That is **2 RTTs per object**, and the server sets up and tears down a connection, with its buffers and state, every time.
text.zh: **非持久 HTTP**：每个对象单独一条 TCP 连接。建立连接（握手一个往返），发请求、收回响应的头几个字节（第二个往返，再加上传完文件的时间），关闭。**每个对象 2 个 RTT**，而且服务器每次都要建立、拆除一条连接及其缓冲区和状态。

text.en: **Persistent HTTP**: the server leaves the connection open after a response, and the next requests to that server use it. One handshake serves the whole page. With **pipelining**, the client sends each request as soon as it finds the reference in the HTML, without waiting for the previous response.
text.zh: **持久 HTTP**：服务器发完响应后不关连接，之后发给这台服务器的请求都走它。整个页面只握一次手。加上**流水线**（pipelining），客户端在 HTML 里一看到引用就发出请求，不必等上一个响应回来。

alt.en: Three client-server timelines for an HTML file and two images. Non-persistent: handshake, request, three times: 6 RTT. Persistent: one handshake, then one request each: 4 RTT. Pipelined: one handshake, the HTML, then both image requests together: 3 RTT.
alt.zh: 一个 HTML 文件加两张图片的三种客户端-服务器时间线。非持久：握手、请求，重复三次：6 个 RTT。持久：握手一次，再每个对象一个请求：4 个 RTT。流水线：握手一次，取 HTML，再把两个图片请求一起发：3 个 RTT。

caption.en: A page with one HTML file and two images, counted in round trips (transmission time left out).
caption.zh: 一个 HTML 文件加两张图片的页面，按往返次数来数（不计传输时间）。

title.en: Counting the round trips of a page
title.zh: 数一个页面要几个往返

say.en: The course's page: an HTML file and 10 images, transmission time left out. **Non-persistent**: each of the 11 objects needs its own handshake and its own request, 2 RTTs each.
say.zh: 课上的页面：一个 HTML 文件加 10 张图片，不计传输时间。**非持久**：11 个对象各要自己的握手和请求，每个 2 个 RTT。

say.en: **Persistent, one request at a time**: one handshake, one round trip for the HTML, then one for each image.
say.zh: **持久，一次一个请求**：握手一次，HTML 一个往返，然后每张图片一个往返。

say.en: **Persistent with pipelining**: the 10 image requests go out together, and their responses come back in about one round trip.
say.zh: **持久加流水线**：10 个图片请求一起发出，它们的响应大约在一个往返里全部回来。

outro.en: TCP gains as well. A connection that stays open keeps the congestion window it has grown; every new connection starts slow start from 1 again (the congestion control lesson).
outro.zh: TCP 本身也受益。一直开着的连接保留着已经长大的拥塞窗口；每条新连接都要从 1 重新慢启动（见拥塞控制那一课）。

prompt.en: Persistent, one request at a time: one handshake, then one round trip per object, for 11 objects. How many RTTs?
prompt.zh: 持久、一次一个请求：握手一次，再每个对象一个往返，一共 11 个对象。几个 RTT？

text.en: A persistent connection has to be closed by someone, some time. The server cannot know whether the user will click another link on this site in two seconds, or never. So it closes a connection that has been idle for a while; the response in the course's slide announces `Keep-Alive: timeout=10`.
text.zh: 持久连接总得有人、在某个时候把它关掉。服务器没法知道用户是两秒后会点这个网站的下一个链接，还是再也不来了。所以它会关掉空闲了一段时间的连接；课件里那个响应写着 `Keep-Alive: timeout=10`。

items.en: **Kept open too long**: every idle connection holds memory, a socket and TCP state on the server. With thousands of visitors, idle connections use up the server's resources and limit how many new clients it can serve.
items.zh: **开得太久**：每条空闲连接都在服务器上占着内存、一个套接字和 TCP 状态。访客成千上万时，空闲连接会耗尽服务器的资源，限制它能服务的新客户端数量。

items.en: **Closed too soon**: the next request must open a new connection, paying the handshake and slow start again, and the benefit is lost.
items.zh: **关得太早**：下一个请求又得建新连接，重新付握手和慢启动的代价，好处就没了。

prompt.en: A busy server keeps idle persistent connections open for ten minutes. What goes wrong?
prompt.zh: 一台很忙的服务器把空闲的持久连接保留十分钟。会出什么问题？

label.en: Thousands of idle connections tie up its memory and sockets, so it struggles to accept new clients
label.zh: 成千上万条空闲连接占着内存和套接字，它很难再接受新客户端

label.en: Pages load more slowly for returning users
label.zh: 回头的用户打开页面更慢

feedback.en: For a user who comes back within ten minutes, the open connection makes the page faster.
feedback.zh: 对十分钟内回来的用户，开着的连接让页面更快。

feedback.en: TCP keeps the order within a connection, however long it stays open.
feedback.zh: 不管连接开多久，TCP 都保证一条连接内的顺序。

explain.en: The cost of a persistent connection is paid by the server while the connection sits idle; the benefit comes only if the client uses it again. The timeout is the trade-off between the two.
explain.zh: 持久连接的代价由服务器在连接空闲期间承担；好处只有客户端再次用到它时才有。超时时间就是在这两者之间的权衡。

text.en: Benefits, each with its reason, then the one challenge, with both sides of it:
text.zh: 先写好处，每条带着理由；再写那一个难点，两面都要说到：

title.zh: 复习课 (2) 第 5 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: Persistent HTTP reuses the same TCP connection for multiple requests and responses between a client and a server. This reduces overhead, since a new TCP connection (with its handshake round trip and the server resources it needs) is not set up for every object, and it increases request throughput and lowers delay, especially with pipelining, where the client sends requests without waiting for each response.
paras.zh: 持久 HTTP 让客户端和服务器之间的多个请求和响应复用同一条 TCP 连接。这减少了开销，因为不必为每个对象新建一条 TCP 连接（以及它的握手往返和所需的服务器资源）；同时提高了请求吞吐量、降低了延迟，在流水线方式下尤其明显——客户端不必等每个响应回来就发出下一个请求。

paras.en: The main challenge is deciding when to close the connection: keeping it open too long wastes server resources on idle connections, while closing it too soon loses the performance benefit, because the next request must open a new connection.
paras.zh: 主要难点是决定什么时候关闭连接：开得太久，空闲连接浪费服务器资源；关得太早，下一个请求又得建新连接，性能上的好处就没了。

title.en: More DNS the exam can ask

text.en: Why not one central DNS server?
text.zh: 为什么不用一台中央 DNS 服务器？

text.en: The course's slide gives four reasons, each worth a sentence: the **traffic volume** of every lookup in the world would swamp one server; it would be a **single point of failure** (the attack in question 4 would need only one target); it would be **distant** from most users, so every lookup would be slow; and one database for every host on Earth would be impossible to **maintain**. A hierarchy of zones spreads the load, the risk and the upkeep, and lets each organisation run its own names.
text.zh: 课件给了四条理由，每条值得写一句：全世界所有查询的**流量**会压垮一台服务器；它会成为**单点故障**（第 4 题里的攻击只需要打一个目标）；它离大多数用户都**很远**，每次查询都慢；一个装着地球上所有主机的数据库根本没法**维护**。按区域分层，把负载、风险和维护工作都分散开，也让每个机构管理自己的名字。

text.en: Recursive and iterative queries
text.zh: 递归查询和迭代查询

text.en: In a **recursive** query, the server asked does all the work and returns the final answer: that is what your computer asks of the local name server. In an **iterative** query, the server asked replies with a referral, *I do not know, but ask this server*: that is how the root, edu and washington.edu servers answer the local name server in the figure above. Lookups run over UDP on port 53, and a lost query is simply sent again.
text.zh: **递归**查询里，被问的服务器包揽所有工作，返回最终答案：你的电脑问本地域名服务器就是这样。**迭代**查询里，被问的服务器只回一个指引：*我不知道，但你去问这台*：上图里根、edu、washington.edu 回答本地域名服务器就是这样。查询走 UDP 的 53 端口，丢了就重发。

title.en: More HTTP the exam can ask

items.en: **Parallel connections.** Browsers also open several non-persistent connections at once to fetch objects in parallel. That cuts the waiting, but multiplies the handshakes and the server's connections.
items.zh: **并行连接。**浏览器也会同时开好几条非持久连接，并行地取对象。这减少了等待，但握手次数和服务器上的连接数都成倍增加。

items.en: **Cookies.** HTTP is stateless: each request stands on its own. A site that wants to recognise you sends `Set-cookie: 1678` once; your browser then adds `Cookie: 1678` to every later request to that site, and the site looks the number up in its database.
items.zh: **Cookie。**HTTP 是无状态的：每个请求都是独立的。网站想认出你，就先发一次 `Set-cookie: 1678`；之后你的浏览器在发往这个网站的每个请求里都带上 `Cookie: 1678`，网站再拿这个号去自己的数据库里查。

items.en: **Web caches** (proxy servers) answer requests with stored copies. They cut response time, network traffic and the load on the origin server; their difficulty is keeping the copies fresh.
items.zh: **网页缓存**（代理服务器）用存下来的副本回答请求。它们缩短响应时间、减少网络流量、减轻源服务器的负担；难处在于让副本保持最新。

title.zh: 你来：非持久地取一个页面

prompt.en: A page has a base HTML file and 5 images, all on one server. With non-persistent HTTP, fetching one object at a time, how many RTTs does the whole page take? (Leave out transmission time.)
prompt.zh: 一个页面有一个基础 HTML 文件和 5 张图片，都在同一台服务器上。用非持久 HTTP、一次取一个对象，整个页面要几个 RTT？（不计传输时间。）

explain.en: 6 objects × 2 RTTs (a handshake and a request each) = 12.
explain.zh: 6 个对象 × 2 个 RTT（各一次握手、一次请求）= 12。

hints.en: Count the objects first, the HTML included.
hints.zh: 先数对象，HTML 也算一个。

title.en: Your turn: the same page, pipelined
title.zh: 你来：同一页面，用流水线

prompt.en: The same page over one persistent connection with pipelining. How many RTTs?
prompt.zh: 同一个页面，用一条持久连接加流水线。几个 RTT？

explain.en: One handshake, one round trip for the HTML, then the 5 image requests together in one more: 3.
explain.zh: 握手一个，HTML 一个，再把 5 个图片请求一起发，又一个：3。

title.en: Your turn: why DNS is spread out
title.zh: 你来：DNS 为什么是分散的

prompt.en: Why is DNS run as a distributed hierarchy of name servers rather than as one central server? Give two reasons.
prompt.zh: DNS 为什么由一个分层的、分布式的域名服务器体系来运行，而不是一台中央服务器？给出两条理由。

key_points.en: One server could not handle the traffic of every lookup
key_points.zh: 一台服务器扛不住所有查询的流量

key_points.en: One server would be a single point of failure
key_points.zh: 一台服务器会成为单点故障

key_points.en: A central server would be far from most users (slow), and one database of every host could not be maintained
key_points.zh: 中央服务器离大多数用户很远（慢），而且一个包含所有主机的数据库无法维护

model_answer.en: A single server would have to answer every lookup in the world, far more traffic than one machine can carry; it would be a single point of failure, so one crash or attack would stop name resolution everywhere; it would be far away from most users, making every lookup slow; and one database of every host would be impossible to keep up to date. A hierarchy of zones spreads the load and the risk, and lets each organisation maintain its own names.
model_answer.zh: 一台服务器得回答全世界的每一次查询，流量远超一台机器的承受能力；它会是单点故障，一次崩溃或攻击就让各地的域名解析全停；它离大多数用户都很远，每次查询都慢；一个包含所有主机的数据库也不可能维护得过来。按区域分层能分散负载和风险，也让每个机构自己维护自己的名字。

explain.en: Any two of: traffic volume, single point of failure, distance, maintenance, each with a word on why.
explain.zh: 四条里任选两条：流量、单点故障、距离、维护，每条说一句为什么。

prompt.en: Looking up robot.cs.washington.edu, the root server answers the local name server with *ask the edu server*. What kind of query is that?
prompt.zh: 查询 robot.cs.washington.edu 时，根服务器回复本地域名服务器：*去问 edu 服务器*。这是哪种查询？

label.en: Iterative: the server replies with a referral instead of the final answer
label.zh: 迭代查询：服务器回复一个指引，而不是最终答案

label.en: Recursive: the root does the work on the asker's behalf
label.zh: 递归查询：根服务器替提问者包办

feedback.en: A recursive server would return the final address itself, as the local name server does for your computer.
feedback.zh: 递归的话，服务器会自己把最终地址找来返回，就像本地域名服务器替你的电脑做的那样。

feedback.en: A cached answer would be the address itself; a referral only says whom to ask next.
feedback.zh: 缓存的答案就是地址本身；指引只说下一个该问谁。

explain.en: Root and top-level servers answer iteratively, which keeps them light: each reply is one step down the tree. The local name server makes the whole walk, recursively on behalf of its users.
explain.zh: 根服务器和顶级域服务器用迭代方式回答，这让它们负担很轻：每次回复只往树下走一步。整条路由本地域名服务器替它的用户递归地走完。
